verdict.calm.title: All calm
verdict.calm.body: No critical issues found in what we can see. Keep PHP and plugins updated.
verdict.mild.title: Mild headache
verdict.mild.body: A few things need attention. None look urgent, but fix them this week.
verdict.major.title: Major headache
verdict.major.body: Something serious is exposed. Fix the critical items today.
verdict.unknown.title: Can't tell yet
verdict.unknown.body: We could not see enough to judge. Details below.
check.EX-01.title: Your .env file is public
check.EX-01.impact: Anyone can download your database password, app key and other secrets.
check.EX-01.fix: Block access to .env files in your web server and serve the site from the public folder. Then change every password and key in that file.
check.EX-02.title: Your .git folder is public
check.EX-02.impact: Anyone can download your source code and its history, including secrets that were ever saved in it.
check.EX-02.fix: Block access to /.git in your web server, or deploy without the .git folder. Change every secret that was ever in the repository.
check.EX-03.title: Your Git config file is public
check.EX-03.impact: It shows your repository address and means the whole .git folder can likely be downloaded.
check.EX-03.fix: Block access to /.git in your web server, or deploy without the .git folder. Change every secret that was ever in the repository.
check.EX-04.title: Your composer.lock file is public
check.EX-04.impact: Attackers can see every package and its exact version, then pick known exploits.
check.EX-04.fix: Serve the site from the public folder so project files cannot be reached, or block composer.* files in your web server.
check.EX-05.title: Your composer.json file is public
check.EX-05.impact: Attackers can see which packages you use, which makes known bugs easier to target.
check.EX-05.fix: Serve the site from the public folder so project files cannot be reached, or block composer.* files in your web server.
check.EX-06.title: Your Laravel log file is public
check.EX-06.impact: Logs often contain error details, file paths, emails and sometimes passwords or tokens.
check.EX-06.fix: Serve the site from the public folder so /storage cannot be reached. Then delete old logs and change any secret found in them.
check.EX-07.title: A phpinfo page is public
check.EX-07.impact: It shows your exact PHP version, server paths and settings, which helps attackers plan an attack.
check.EX-07.fix: Delete the phpinfo file from your server.
check.EX-08.title: Laravel Ignition debug tools are public
check.EX-08.impact: Old Ignition versions let anyone run code on your server (CVE-2021-3129).
check.EX-08.fix: Set APP_DEBUG=false in production and update facade/ignition or spatie/laravel-ignition to the latest version.
check.EX-09.title: PHPUnit's eval-stdin.php file is reachable
check.EX-09.impact: This file lets anyone run code on your server (CVE-2017-9841). Bots look for it every day.
check.EX-09.fix: Deploy without dev packages (composer install --no-dev) and block /vendor in your web server.
check.EX-10.title: A Laravel Telescope or Horizon dashboard is public
check.EX-10.impact: Anyone can see requests, database queries, jobs and user data from your app.
check.EX-10.fix: Protect the dashboard with its authorization gate in production, or turn it off.
check.EX-11.title: A database admin tool is public
check.EX-11.impact: Attackers can try to guess your database login, and old versions have known bugs.
check.EX-11.fix: Remove Adminer or phpMyAdmin from the public site, or allow only your own IP address.
check.EX-12.title: A backup or database dump is public
check.EX-12.impact: Anyone can download your code or your whole database, including customer data.
check.EX-12.fix: Delete backup files from the web folder and keep backups outside it. Treat the data as leaked.
